findings.description: The bucket has no ACL or public access block configuration and is explicitly commented as public, exposing potentially sensitive customer data (customer-master.xlsx) to unauthenticated or unintended access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket, including customer data, are not encrypted at rest.

Versioning is not enabled, increasing the risk of accidental or malicious data loss/overwrite with no recovery path, compounded by force_destroy being true which permits deletion of a non-empty bucket.
A customer master data file is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer records to unauthorized access and cleartext storage.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving sensitive data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so data in this bucket is stored unencrypted despite versioning being enabled.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so data in this bucket is stored unencrypted despite having logging and versioning enabled.
